comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C8, C68-C72 regarding multi-omics integration and Western blot validation. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergent evidence across multiple levels, while peer reviewers commend the confirmational data and thorough integration with prior work.

Perfect agreement on claims C74-C77 regarding discordance analysis between phosphorylation and expression levels. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the methodological soundness and biological insight, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the comprehensive dataset demonstrating thorough analysis.

Both evaluations rate claims C9, C16 (main conclusions about resilience/adaptation) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the link is inferential rather than experimentally demonstrated, requiring perturbation experiments. Peer reviewers similarly express concern about premature mechanistic conclusions, noting the study generates hypotheses rather than testing them, though they don't directly challenge the resilience claim.

Perfect agreement on claims C27-C28 regarding absence of pathological hypertrophy. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED based on prior work (Tarasov 2022). OpenEval notes this creates a paradox with activated hypertrophy signaling, while peer reviewers accept the adaptive nature without questioning the apparent contradiction.

Strong agreement on claims C1, C10-C12 regarding TGAC8 model background. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as appropriate citations to prior work. OpenEval emphasizes the importance for interpreting findings, while peer reviewers accept the rationale but note concerns about relevance to human disease (C15 in peer review).

Strong agreement on claims C2, C17, C21-C22 regarding phosphoproteomic profiling and PCA analysis. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of the mass spectrometry data and statistical approaches, while peer reviewers commend the unbiased analysis and acknowledge differences between groups.

Both address phosphoproteomics findings. OpenEval R1 covers C18, C23-C24 (upregulated phosphoproteins, statistical cutoffs) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 also finds C18, C23-C24 SUPPORTED, accepting the directionality and magnitude without challenge. Complete agreement on these overlapping claims.

Both address normalization analysis (C65-C67) and correlation analyses. OpenEval finds C65-C67 SUPPORTED, emphasizing the importance of the control analysis. Peer R8 covers broader correlation claims (C50-C51, C65-C67) and praises the innovative cross-analyses approach. Both evaluations are positive about the integrative methodology.

Both address correlation analyses C50-C51. OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical quantification showing transcriptome-phosphoproteome and proteome-phosphoproteome correlations. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, praising the innovative cross-analyses linking different omics levels.

Both address pathway activation claims. OpenEval R2 rates C3, C25 as UNCERTAIN due to contradiction between pathway activation and lack of phenotypic hypertrophy. Peer R3 finds C3, C25 (along with C4, C5, C43, C48-C49) SUPPORTED, treating pathway enrichment as a core finding without methodological concerns. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

Both address functional enrichment claims C5, C48-C49. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by IPA analysis but notes the causal link to adaptation is inferential. Peer R3 finds these SUPPORTED as part of comprehensive pathway analysis, explicitly affirming stress-response, immune, and metabolic pathway activation without expressing concerns about inferential nature.

Both address kinase predictions. OpenEval R4 rates C4, C38-C39, C43 as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing reliance on computational predictions without experimental validation. Peer R3 finds these claims (along with C3, C5, C25, C48-C49) SUPPORTED, treating pathway findings as thorough and well-integrated. Disagreement on sufficiency of computational evidence.

Both address kinase findings. OpenEval R4 rates C4, C38-C39, C43 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation of predicted kinase activities. Peer R4 finds C6, C37-C39, C52-C53 SUPPORTED, accepting computational predictions and motif analysis as part of the comprehensive dataset. Disagreement on validation requirements.

Both address regulatory proteins. OpenEval R9 finds C52-C53 SUPPORTED by phosphoproteomics data with appropriate statistical thresholds. Peer R4 also finds C52-C53 (along with C6, C37-C39) SUPPORTED, accepting the findings as part of the innovative cross-analyses approach. Agreement on these specific claims.

Both address motif analysis. OpenEval R3 finds C35-C37 SUPPORTED with robust bioinformatic validation of phosphorylation motifs. Peer R4 finds C37 (along with C6, C38-C39, C52-C53) SUPPORTED as part of the comprehensive dataset. Agreement on motif analysis validity.

Both address kinase/phosphatase predictions. OpenEval R10 rates C54-C56 as UNCERTAIN, noting predictions are computational without direct measurement of activation states. Peer R5 finds C54-C56 (along with C7, C57-C58, C60, C62) SUPPORTED, accepting the integrated multi-omics analysis without challenging computational predictions. Disagreement on validation requirements.

Both address transcription factor regulation. OpenEval R11 rates C57-C62 as UNCERTAIN, noting the sumoylation coordination hypothesis (C62) is speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer R5 finds C57-C58, C60, C62 (along with C7, C54-C56) SUPPORTED, accepting the connection between phosphorylation and transcriptional activation. Disagreement on sufficiency of pathway analysis for mechanistic claims.

OpenEval R5 rates C40-C42 as UNCERTAIN, noting the PDPK1 link is speculative based on studies in other cell types without cardiac-specific validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific claims about PDPK1 extrapolation from glioblastoma and myoblast studies.

OpenEval R7 rates C44-C47 regarding GSK3B phosphorylation as UNCERTAIN, noting kinase assignments are based on prior studies in other systems rather than direct evidence in this cardiac model. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses GSK3B phosphorylation claims.

OpenEval R12 rates C63-C64 as UNCERTAIN, noting GO analysis supports C63 but C64 relies on IPA predictions without experimental validation of kinase activation states. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims about mitochondrial protein phosphorylation and kinase predictions.

OpenEval R15 finds C73 SUPPORTED, noting substrate mapping provides functional evidence for AKT pathway activation beyond measuring AKT phosphorylation itself. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses AKT substrate phosphorylation mapping.

OpenEval R18 rates C29-C33 regarding RyR2 as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are based on citations to prior studies without experimental validation in this system. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses RyR2 phosphorylation and calcium handling claims.

OpenEval R21 finds C78-C82 regarding STAT phosphorylation SUPPORTED, appropriately integrating prior literature with current phosphoproteomics findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses STAT1/3 phosphorylation claims.
